summary: The 2026 Iran war (the US and Israel against Iran, since Feb 28) is in a tense pause: there are no confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks, but Iran is still attacking ships around the Strait of Hormuz, the US blockade of Iranian ports continues, and talks on a new draft deal are under way. Hormuz is open only in part, with oil flows well below normal.

status.label: Strait of Hormuz
status.note: Iran says it is closed to ships that don't coordinate with its Persian Gulf Strait Authority; the US says the main routes are open under US control. Most ships now pass through a US-run transit system (101 transits over Oct 22–24, against about 138 a day in 2025), with only a handful a day outside it.

status.label: Oil through Hormuz
status.note: Around 11.6 to 11.7 million barrels a day in October, against about 17.1 million before the war (Kpler).

status.label: The war
status.note: No confirmed US or Israeli strikes on Iran in recent weeks (AFP reported none on Iranian targets since early September). Trump said on Oct 8 the US would not resume strikes before the Nov 3 midterms; reports say renewed strikes are being prepared for after that.

status.label: Brent crude
status.note: Brent for January settled at US$113.43 on Friday Oct 30, up US$2.63; the expired December contract settled at US$117.64. WTI settled at US$104.12. Brent rose 13.6% in October, a fourth straight monthly gain (Reuters, via CNBC and FinanceFeeds).

updates.text: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that Tehran had studied a letter from US Vice President JD Vance, called the US attempt to open dialogue a 'positive step', and said an Iranian delegation is in Doha for talks with mediators.

Saudi air defences said they intercepted a drone over the Riyadh region and two more over the Eastern and Southern regions on Oct 31; the coalition said the one aimed at the Southern Region was launched by the Houthis. No injuries were reported.
Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said there are currently no plans for meetings with American officials.
State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott warned Iran there 'will be consequences' if its attacks continue; AP, citing two diplomats, reported Trump has not made a final decision on renewed strikes.

UK Maritime Trade Operations recorded more than 30 attacks on commercial ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October, the highest monthly total of the war and more than double September's; it has recorded 145 incidents since the war began.
Oman's Maritime Security Center said its navy rescued 25 crew from the Panama-flagged tanker RITI after it was attacked and caught fire; the crew received medical care.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said four oil tankers caught fire and exploded in the Strait of Hormuz, saying the ships had used 'unauthorised routes'; the cause has not been independently confirmed.
Trump said the war with Iran will be 'wrapped up soon', as Qatari mediators returned to Tehran in a push for a deal.

background: The war began on Feb 28, 2026 with US and Israeli strikes on Iran. An April ceasefire collapsed on July 8. The US has blockaded Iranian ports since April (reinstated in July); Iran restricts and attacks shipping through Hormuz, which carried about a fifth of the world's oil before the war.
factcheck: Checked by Claude against at least two reputable sources where possible. Statements by Iran's military, the US military (CENTCOM) or President Trump are labelled as claims, because each side's account of who controls the strait differs.
